proof_attempt_summary: The run proved proper inclusion of the actual nonsingular Gaussian models and their Zariski closures for an explicit maximal-arid four-vertex pair, then separated the positive nested-Markov models on every common finite product state space by exact state splitting. It also proved four-vertex minimality and characterized the exact positive binary intersection; both substantive D0.5 panels passed with no findings. The result missed the field floor only on breadth: a general forbidden-pattern characterization or inclusion-testing method remains open, as does the deliberately excluded Gaussian-equivalence-only implication.
tldr: Does inclusion of Gaussian covariance varieties faithfully reflect inclusion of positive nonparametric nested-Markov models for maximal arid graphs? We prove that it does not. A vertex-minimal four-variable pair has a constructive proper inclusion of its entire nonsingular Gaussian source model, yet state-splitting one exact interior binary witness separates the positive nested models on every common finite product state space with at least two states per variable. The binary channel-symmetry theorem explains the exceptional source laws that remain target-compatible. Because the Gaussian inclusion is strict, Gaussian-equivalence-only transfer remains open.
gap: Van Ommen (2024) proves that nested inclusion implies Gaussian algebraic inclusion and conjectures the converse. That converse would allow efficient covariance-algebra algorithms to decide nonparametric nested inclusion, but the literature does not establish that a Gaussian slice is order-reflecting.
fill: Prove a smallest proper-inclusion counterexample, verify it by a positive-definite Gaussian reparameterization and an interior rational binary witness, and derive an if-and-only-if description of the exceptional binary source laws that remain target-compatible.
